title: Composable Retention Scenarios & Evidence Orchestrator for Streaming Requests
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Customers that use streaming or long-lived chat sessions need fine-grained retention controls that understand session windows, partial-token flushes, and KV/prefix caching. Existing route-level TTLs treat streamed requests like discrete events which leads to either over-retention of sensitive prefixes or complex manual work to stitch evidence exports for compliance audits.

Goal: Provide a Composer + Orchestrator UX + API that lets PMs/Platform engineers define composable retention scenarios (route + session window + token-class filters), simulate retention outcomes for streaming workloads, and produce forensic-ready evidence bundles on demand or via automated export hooks. The solution must work for prompts, responses, request logs, and derived metrics and integrate with the runtime's prefix/KV cache semantics so exported evidence matches what the runtime actually persisted/sharded.
acceptance_criteria: Scenario Composer UI: create/preview up to 5 composable rules (route, session-window, token-class, sampling, emergency-override) and save to policy library
Simulator: run synthetic streaming traces and output per-route retention delta estimates (counts, bytes) with a 5% accuracy tolerance vs runtime telemetry
Forensic Evidence API: export a signed bundle that contains request artifacts, retention policy snapshot, provenance metadata, and an integrity hash manifest
Runtime hooks: retention decisions exercised in staging that respect prefix/KV caching and result in identical eviction artifacts as those produced by the orchestration exports
Automated export: scheduled or event-triggered evidence exports for legal-hold and region-aware residency with retry/backoff and audit logs
updates: 2026-03-12 - Ticket created by Aisha Kumar. Drafted scope with compliance and runtime leads. Initial UX sketches attached to linked Confluence doc.
2026-03-13 - Scoped simulator requirements with Runtime team (Liam O'Connor). Decided to model both prefix-cache hits and partial flush windows to match streaming workloads.

2026-03-14 - Product/Legal sync: add mandatory provenance metadata (policy version, signer, KMS key id) to evidence bundles. Marked security_review_required=true. Assigned to Mei Chen for PM ownership. Engineering spike planned in cycle 2026-W12.
tasks: Design: final Composer wireframes and compact policy expression UX (DES-xxxxx)
Engineering Spike: simulator prototype and synthetic trace harness (ENG-xxxxx)
Runtime: add retention decision hooks for prefix/KV cache inspection and stable snapshot API (ENG-xxxxx)
Security: define KMS/HSM signing pattern and access controls for evidence exports
Docs: author 'Evidence bundle format' spec and export troubleshooting guide
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Evidence exports may diverge from runtime state if retention hooks lag or compaction runs concurrently. Mitigation: implement operation-safe snapshot API and record compaction watermark in manifest.
Risk: Large streaming workloads can produce evidence bundles exceeding export quotas. Mitigation: introduce sampled attachments, chunked export, and presigned S3 streaming with resumable uploads.
Risk: Cross-region residency constraints conflict with global exports. Mitigation: policy validation step that flags region-violating exports and requires explicit approval.
notes: We should align the policy DSL with the existing RPEL effort but extend it with 'session_window' and 'prefix_class' operators for streaming semantics.
Prototype simulator must accept real request schemas (prompt/response/token-level annotations) so accuracy tests use production traces anonymized via the telemetry pipeline.
Consider a minimal 'forensic API' v1 with signed manifest and an 'evidence-lite' mode for low-cost exports that includes hashed pointers to archived payloads.
